Travis CI is part of 25 of my public repositories, from 2013 to 2021.

What it was for: [Learning and experiments](@/projects/learning.md) (11), [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (4), [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (4) and [Science and visualisation](@/projects/science.md) (3).

Most recently: [maze-rs](@/work/maze-rs.md): Maze generation algorithms from the book, in Rust; [rustas](@/work/rustas.md): Rust - Assembler, Mathematics, GPU and many others; [rustler-test](@/work/rustler-test.md): Working Example of Rustler - Safe Rust bridge for creating Erlang NIF functions.

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Travis CI: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Travis CI to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
